context: Zoomable treemap of a synthetic file system with 471 files across 8 top-level directories, using area to encode file sizes with click-to-zoom interaction.
first_impression: Structurally honest treemap with correct area-proportional encoding and data-driven layout, but a few minor integrity gaps.
what_works: Area encoding is mathematically correct — d3.treemap().size() derives layout from summed leaf values, so areas are proportional to file sizes with no baseline or radius-deception issues. Zoom uses data-driven x/y scale domains (target.x0/x1, y0/y1) rather than hardcoded values.
what_doesnt: Legend swatches show raw palette colors but cells render HCL-adjusted variants (lightness/chroma modified per depth), creating a visual mismatch that undermines the legend's utility. Leaf cell lightness includes `rng() * 10` random variation — color differences encode nothing but may imply data meaning to users.
